theory.overview: A queue is a linear data structure that follows the First In First Out (FIFO) principle. The first element added is the first one to be removed. Think of it like a line of people - the person who arrived first is served first. Queues support enqueue (add to rear) and dequeue (remove from front) operations. They are essential for task scheduling, breadth-first search, caching, and handling requests in order.

keyConcepts.name: FIFO Principle
keyConcepts.description: First In, First Out - the oldest element in the queue is processed first. This ensures fairness in task scheduling.

keyConcepts.name: Enqueue and Dequeue
keyConcepts.description: Enqueue adds to the rear (tail). Dequeue removes from the front (head). Both are O(1) operations in a proper implementation.

keyConcepts.name: Front and Rear Pointers
keyConcepts.description: Front tracks where elements are removed. Rear tracks where elements are added. These pointers move as operations occur.

keyConcepts.name: Circular Queue
keyConcepts.description: An efficient implementation using an array where the rear can wrap around to the beginning when space is available at the front.

problems.title: As Far from Land as Possible

algorithmSteps.description: Enqueue 10: Add to rear of queue
Enqueue 20: Rear pointer moves to index 1
Dequeue: Remove 10 from front, front pointer moves
Peek: View front element (20) without removing

minigame.title: Build the Queue
minigame.description: Use Enqueue and Dequeue operations to transform [1, 2, 3] into [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. Remember: Queue is FIFO!
instructions: Use Enqueue to add elements to rear
Use Dequeue to remove from front
Match the target queue to win
